advances: This gives a parameter-uniform, finite piecewise-algebraic capacity-certified lower envelope for the third endpoint contribution.  At the target allowance \(\eta=t-c_3\), one exact finite minimum \(\Gamma_\eta\) decides a sufficient subregion: \(\Gamma_\eta\ge0\) implies that the third row has mass at least \(t\), with no restriction on determinant signs, cap-order cells, repeated values, or minimum-attainment choices.  Exact rational data with endpoint contribution zero show that the displayed third-row and incidence-chamber hypotheses alone do not imply the budget; the remaining step for this route is to prove that the first two strict row inequalities force \(\Gamma_\eta\ge0\).
author: r122-contained-envelope
proof:
We first normalize every compatible endpoint pair without choosing a minimum-attaining column.  Put
\[
\ell_i=\min_jU_{ij},\qquad
n_i=\min_jV_{ij},\qquad
\ell=(\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3)^{\mathsf T},\qquad
s=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\ell.
\tag{25}
\]
Column stochasticity and \(\det U\ne0\) give \(s<1\): if \(s=1\), every nonnegative column of \(U-\ell\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\) has sum zero, so all columns of \(U\) equal \(\ell\).  Similarly \(\sum_i n_i<1\).  Summing (3) gives \(s\ge-\sum_i n_i>-1\).  Thus
\[
X=\frac{U-\ell\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}}{1-s},
\qquad
Y=\frac{V+\ell\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}}{1+s}
\tag{26}
\]
are entrywise nonnegative and column stochastic.  Writing \(x=1-s\),
\[
U=\ell\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}+xX,qquad
V=-\ell\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}+(2-x)Y.
\tag{27}
\]
The determinant lemma, using \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}X=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}Y=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\), gives
\[
|\det X|=\frac A{x^2}=:\alpha,
\qquad
|\det Y|=\frac B{(2-x)^2}=:\beta.
\tag{28}
\]
The images \(T_X=X\Delta\) and \(T_Y=Y\Delta\) are subtriangles of \(\Delta\), so \(\alpha,\beta\le1\).  This proves (5) and also shows that the two arguments in (7) are less than one.

Put \(\delta=g\ell+\sigma_3\) and
\[
r=-\frac\delta x,\qquad z=\frac\delta{2-x}.
\tag{29}
\]
Equation (27), translation by a multiple of \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\), and positive homogeneity give
\[
\rho_X:=\mathcal C(gU;-\sigma_3)=\mathcal C(gX;r),
\qquad
\rho_Y:=\mathcal C(gV;\sigma_3)=\mathcal C(gY;z),
\tag{30}
\]
and the allocation identity is
\[
x r+(2-x)z=0.
\tag{31}
\]

We need two elementary triangle facts.  First, if \(T\) is a nondegenerate triangle of area \(\theta\), \(f\) is affine on \(T\), and the upper cap \(T\cap\{f\ge q\}\) has area fraction \(0\le\rho<1\), then the lower part \(T\cap\{f\le q\}\) contains a triangle of area at least
\[
\theta(1-\sqrt\rho).
\tag{32}
\]
For \(\rho=0\), the whole triangle is in the lower halfspace.  Otherwise the complete cap cells of accepted fact `64760c76cadff481` leave two possibilities.  If the upper cap is a corner triangle with edge ratios \(r_1,r_2\), then \(\rho=r_1r_2\), while the complementary quadrilateral contains a triangle of area fraction \(1-\min\{r_1,r_2\}\ge1-\sqrt\rho\).  If the lower cap is a corner triangle, its fraction is \(1-\rho\ge1-\sqrt\rho\).  This includes cuts through vertices, repeated vertex values, and the constant case.

Second, for
\[
K_q=\{\lambda\in\Delta:g\lambda\le q\},
\]
the maximum normalized area of a triangle contained in \(K_q\) is
\[
m(q)=
\begin{cases}
0,&q\le-d,\\[1mm]
\dfrac{(q+d)^2}{(d-e)(p+d)},&-d\le q\le-e,\\[3mm]
\dfrac{q+d}{p+d},&-e\le q\le p,\\[3mm]
1,&q\ge p.
\end{cases}
\tag{33}
\]
When \(d=e\), the second branch is omitted and the third branch begins at
\(q=-d\).
The quadratic branch is the similar corner triangle at the \(-d\) vertex.  In the next branch \(K_q\) is the quadrilateral obtained by cutting off the \(p\) vertex.  A maximum-area inscribed triangle can be moved vertex by vertex to polygon vertices.  The four resulting area fractions are
\[
u,\quad v,\quad u(1-v),\quad v(1-u),
\qquad
u=\frac{q+d}{p+d},\quad v=\frac{q+e}{p+e},
\]
and \(0<v<u<1\), so the maximum is \(u\).  The endpoint values agree, and the case \(d=e\) is the limiting formula with no quadratic interval.  Inverting (33) gives the exact implication
\[
m(q)>w\quad\Longrightarrow\quad q>\psi(w)
\qquad(0\le w<1).
\tag{34}
\]

Suppose now that the conclusion of (9) fails, so
\[
A\rho_X+B\rho_Y<\varepsilon.
\tag{35}
\]
Then \(\rho_X<\varepsilon/A\) and \(\rho_Y<\varepsilon/B\).  Applying (32) inside \(T_X,T_Y\), and then (34), gives strictly
\[
r>\psi\left(\alpha\left(1-\sqrt{\frac\varepsilon A}\right)\right)
=\psi\left(\frac{\mu_\varepsilon}{x^2}\right),
\tag{36}
\]
\[
z>\psi\left(\beta\left(1-\sqrt{\frac\varepsilon B}\right)\right)
=\psi\left(\frac{\nu_\varepsilon}{(2-x)^2}\right).
\tag{37}
\]
Multiplying by \(x,2-x>0\) and using (31) yields
\[
0>G_\varepsilon(x)\ge\Gamma_\varepsilon.
\tag{38}
\]
This contradicts \(\Gamma_\varepsilon\ge0\), proving (9).

For the finite evaluation, direct substitution into (1) gives whenever
\(q>0,r>0\) and \(q/r^2\in[0,1]\),
\[
r\psi(q/r^2)
=-dr+\max\left\{
\sqrt{q(d-e)(p+d)},\frac{(p+d)q}{r}
\right\}=H_q(r).
\tag{39}
\]
This proves (11).  Partition \(I\) at the two switch points in (13).  Where both reciprocal terms in (10) are active, the unique stationary point is the third point in (12).  Where exactly one reciprocal term is active, the sum is respectively decreasing or increasing.  Where neither is active, it is constant.  Thus a minimum occurs at an endpoint, a switch point, or that stationary point, proving (14).

For fixed \(x\), \(G_\varepsilon(x)\) is nonincreasing in \(\varepsilon\), because \(\mu_\varepsilon,\nu_\varepsilon\) decrease and \(\psi\) increases.  If \(E(U,V,\sigma_3)<E_{\rm cap}\), the definition of the supremum supplies \(\varepsilon>E(U,V,\sigma_3)\) with \(\Gamma_\varepsilon\ge0\), contradicting (9).  This proves (16).  Accepted fact `7d66445eba62df98` proves \(0<\eta<4A/9<A<B\) in the contained chamber, so substituting \(\varepsilon=\eta\) proves (18).

It remains to verify the exact obstruction.  Let
\[
X=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&0&12/25\\
1&0&13/25\\
0&1&0
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\ell=\frac16(1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{40}
\]
Then \(\det X=12/25\), and (21) is exactly
\[
U=\ell\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}+\frac12X,
\qquad
V=-\ell\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}+\frac32X.
\tag{41}
\]
Hence their columns sum to one and
\[
\det U=\frac14\det X=\frac3{25}=A,
\qquad
\det V=\frac94\det X=\frac{27}{25}=B.
\tag{42}
\]
Every row minimum of \(U\) is \(1/6\), and every row minimum of \(V\) is \(-1/6\), so (3) holds with equality.  Also
\[
gX=(-940,-56,-44/5),\qquad g\ell=\frac23.
\tag{43}
\]
With \(\sigma_3=-2/3\),
\[
gU+\sigma_3\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}=\frac12gX<0,
\qquad
gV-\sigma_3\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}=\frac32gX<0
\tag{44}
\]
entrywise.  Both cap fractions in (22) are therefore zero.  The one-positive formula of accepted fact `64760c76cadff481` gives (20).  The residual normalized data are \(R=A/B=1/9\), \(S=1/B=25/27\), so \(1-R<S<1+R\).  Also \(R<(27-2\sqrt{26})/25\), and hence all strict residual area inequalities hold.

Finally, direct calculation from (21) gives
\[
U\bar\lambda=(37/150,21/50,1/3)^{\mathsf T},\qquad
V\bar\lambda=(11/150,89/150,1/3)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
For (23),
\[
L\bar\lambda=(-1/12,-1/4,4/3)^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
LU\bar\lambda+\sigma
=(4171/12,19573/60,-2512/15)^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
LV\bar\lambda-\sigma
=(-13/12,-17/20,-2512/5)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus all asserted centroid signs, (24), \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\sigma=1516/3>1\), the column-sum identity, and invertibility are literal.  Compatibility of the three transformed triangles follows from (3) by the exact equivalence in accepted fact `64760c76cadff481`.  This completes both the envelope proof and the complementary obstruction.
statement:
Let
\[
\Delta=\operatorname{conv}\{e_1,e_2,e_3\},\qquad
\mathcal C(w;\tau)=|\{\lambda\in\Delta:w\lambda\ge\tau\}|,
\qquad |\Delta|=1,
\]
and let
\[
g=(p,-a,-b),\qquad p,a,b>0.
\]
Put
\[
d=\max\{a,b\},\qquad e=\min\{a,b\},\qquad
h=\frac{d-e}{p+d}.
\]
For \(0\le w\le1\), define
\[
\psi(w)=
\begin{cases}
-d+\sqrt{w(d-e)(p+d)},&0\le w\le h,\\[1mm]
(p+d)w-d,&h\le w\le1.
\end{cases}
\tag{1}
\]
The two formulas agree at \(h\); when \(d=e\), the first branch consists only of \(w=0\).

Let \(A,B>0\).  For every pair \(U,V\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}\) satisfying
\[
\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}U=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T},\qquad
\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}V=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T},\qquad
|\det U|=A,\qquad |\det V|=B,
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
\min_jU_{ij}+\min_jV_{ij}\ge0\qquad(i=1,2,3),
\tag{3}
\]
define, for \(\sigma_3\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E(U,V,\sigma_3)
=A\mathcal C(gU;-\sigma_3)+B\mathcal C(gV;\sigma_3).
\tag{4}
\]
Existence of such a pair implies
\[
I=[\sqrt A,\,2-\sqrt B]\ne\varnothing.
\tag{5}
\]
For \(0<\varepsilon<\min\{A,B\}\), put
\[
\mu_\varepsilon=A\left(1-\sqrt{\frac\varepsilon A}\right),\qquad
\nu_\varepsilon=B\left(1-\sqrt{\frac\varepsilon B}\right)
\tag{6}
\]
and
\[
G_\varepsilon(x)
=x\psi\left(\frac{\mu_\varepsilon}{x^2}\right)
+(2-x)\psi\left(\frac{\nu_\varepsilon}{(2-x)^2}\right)
\qquad(x\in I).
\tag{7}
\]
Both arguments of \(\psi\) lie in \([0,1)\).  Define
\[
\Gamma_\varepsilon=\min_{x\in I}G_\varepsilon(x).
\tag{8}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{\ \Gamma_\varepsilon\ge0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
E(U,V,\sigma_3)\ge\varepsilon
\text{ for every }(U,V,\sigma_3)\text{ satisfying (2)--(3).}\ }
\tag{9}
\]

The minimum in (8) is a finite algebraic expression, not an unevaluated optimization problem.  For \(q>0,r>0\), set
\[
H_q(r)=-dr+
\max\left\{
\sqrt{q(d-e)(p+d)},\frac{(p+d)q}{r}
\right\}.
\tag{10}
\]
Then
\[
G_\varepsilon(x)=H_{\mu_\varepsilon}(x)
+H_{\nu_\varepsilon}(2-x).
\tag{11}
\]
Let \(\mathcal X_\varepsilon\) contain the points of
\[
\left\{
\sqrt A,\ 2-\sqrt B,\
\frac{2\sqrt{\mu_\varepsilon}}
{\sqrt{\mu_\varepsilon}+\sqrt{\nu_\varepsilon}}
\right\}
\tag{12}
\]
that lie in \(I\).  If \(d>e\), also include, when they lie in \(I\),
\[
\sqrt{\frac{\mu_\varepsilon(p+d)}{d-e}},
\qquad
2-\sqrt{\frac{\nu_\varepsilon(p+d)}{d-e}}.
\tag{13}
\]
Then exactly
\[
\boxed{\ \Gamma_\varepsilon
=\min_{x\in\mathcal X_\varepsilon}
\left(H_{\mu_\varepsilon}(x)+H_{\nu_\varepsilon}(2-x)\right).\ }
\tag{14}
\]
Consequently the exact capacity envelope
\[
E_{\rm cap}(p,a,b;A,B)
=\sup\left(
\{0\}\cup
\left\{\varepsilon\in(0,\min\{A,B\}):
\Gamma_\varepsilon\ge0\right\}
\right)
\tag{15}
\]
satisfies
\[
E(U,V,\sigma_3)\ge E_{\rm cap}(p,a,b;A,B).
\tag{16}
\]

In the contained chamber of accepted fact `7d66445eba62df98`, put
\[
t=\frac{2(1+A+B)}9,\qquad
c_3=\frac{p^2}{(p+a)(p+b)},\qquad
\eta=t-c_3.
\tag{17}
\]
There \(0<\eta<4A/9<A<B\).  Hence (9) applies at \(\varepsilon=\eta\), and
\[
\boxed{\ \Gamma_\eta\ge0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
A\mathcal C(gU;-\sigma_3)+B\mathcal C(gV;\sigma_3)
\ge t-c_3.\ }
\tag{18}
\]

The condition \(\Gamma_\eta\ge0\) cannot be deleted if only the displayed area, third-row, and centroid-incidence hypotheses are retained.  Exact complementary data are
\[
A=\frac3{25},\qquad B=\frac{27}{25},\qquad
g=(1000,-940,-56),\qquad
t=\frac{22}{45},
\tag{19}
\]
for which
\[
p-a-b=4>3,\qquad
c_3=\frac{3125}{6402}>\frac49,\qquad
\eta=t-c_3=\frac{73}{96030}>0.
\tag{20}
\]
Let
\[
U=
\begin{pmatrix}
1/6&1/6&61/150\\
2/3&1/6&32/75\\
1/6&2/3&1/6
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
V=
\begin{pmatrix}
-1/6&-1/6&83/150\\
4/3&-1/6&46/75\\
-1/6&4/3&-1/6
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \sigma_3=-\frac23.
\tag{21}
\]
Then (2)--(3) hold and
\[
A\mathcal C(gU;-\sigma_3)+B\mathcal C(gV;\sigma_3)=0<\eta.
\tag{22}
\]
Moreover these endpoint matrices admit full rational contained-support incidence data
\[
L=
\begin{pmatrix}
-500&500&-1/4\\
-499&441&229/4\\
1000&-940&-56
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\sigma=(261,245,-2/3)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{23}
\]
The columns of \(L\) sum to one, \(\det L=86485\), its row supports are
\[
J_1=\{2\},\qquad J_2=\{2,3\},\qquad J_3=\{1\},
\tag{24}
\]
and its transformed centroids have exactly the contained-support incidence signs.  The data (19)--(24) are not asserted to satisfy the first two strict row-mass inequalities.  They prove that those inequalities, or a consequence of them forcing \(\Gamma_\eta\ge0\), are indispensable for extending (18) to the full surviving chamber.
